title: Shadow traffic: pipeline capacity estimates (ingestion + scoring) — v0.3
body:
Purpose
- Size the ingest + scoring pipeline for shadow traffic so we meet freshness goals without risking user path.
- Provide concrete numbers for: expected sampled QPS, event volume, queue sizing, worker/GPU needs, and the backpressure/circuit-breaker plan.

Context / guardrails we are sizing to
- Shadowing is fail-open: control path must never wait on ingestion/scoring.
- Defaults (per SRE guardrails): sampling 0.5% recommended, max 2.0% without approval, max 2 shadow targets per request.
- Circuit breaker trips if scoring queue oldest-age > 30 minutes (mirroring disabled for affected cohort).
- Scoring SLO: p50 lag <= 10 min, p95 lag <= 60 min (note breaker is stricter than p95).

Assumptions (tunable; used for estimates below)
A. Traffic mix in scope (v1)
- Request types eligible for shadow scoring: chat + completions.
- Embeddings/rerank: mirrored eventing OK, but scoring disabled by default (no rubric benefit).
- Streaming: included; partial captures may result in some score jobs skipped (skipped_no_artifact).

B. Sampling and targets
- s = sampling_rate (default 0.005)
- t = number_of_shadow_targets (default 1; max 2)
- shadow_pairs_per_second ≈ QPS_total * s * t

C. Telemetry event sizes (post normalization + compression; rough)
- shadow.pair.v1: 0.6 KB avg (range 0.4–1.2 KB depending on token/cost fields present)
- shadow.score.v1: 0.7 KB avg (range 0.5–1.0 KB; bounded allowlist)
- Note: artifacts (prompt/response) are NOT in these events; only artifact_ref.

D. Scoring model (v1 rubric: quality-v1)
We model scoring as two components:
1) Heuristics (CPU): format adherence checks, length/empty checks, simple refusal markers
- CPU_time_per_job: 25 ms (p95 60 ms)
2) Model-graded (GPU) (for instruction_following.score + optional safety classifier when enabled)
- gpu_fraction = fraction of jobs that run model-graded (default 0.25 for beta; configurable per route)
- GPU_time_per_graded_job: 250 ms (L4-class GPU, batched; p95 450 ms)
- Effective GPU_time_per_job = gpu_fraction * GPU_time_per_graded_job
  - with gpu_fraction=0.25 => ~62.5 ms GPU/job (effective)

E. Peaks
- Peak-to-average factor: 2.0x (conservative) for ingestion and queue depth.
- We size workers for peak and use autoscaling with a floor.


1) Volume model (events/sec, GB/day)
Formulas
- pair_events_per_second = QPS_total * s * t
- score_events_per_second ≈ pair_events_per_second * score_coverage
  - score_coverage defaults to 0.95 (some skips due to missing artifacts, timeouts, etc.)
- ingest_kb_per_second ≈ (pair_eps * 0.6) + (score_eps * 0.7)
- ingest_gb_per_day ≈ ingest_kb_per_second * 86400 / 1e6

Scenario table (per region; multiply by regions as needed)

| Scenario | QPS_total (eligible) | s | t | pair_eps | score_eps (95%) | ingest_kB/s | ingest_GB/day |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| S1: Dedicated beta route (single tenant) | 1,500 | 0.005 | 1 | 7.5 | 7.1 | 9.4 | 0.81 |
| S2: Dedicated beta tenant (multiple routes) | 3,000 | 0.005 | 1 | 15.0 | 14.3 | 18.8 | 1.62 |
| S3: Busy Hosted region (aggregate) | 20,000 | 0.005 | 1 | 100.0 | 95.0 | 126.5 | 10.9 |
| S4: Approved high sample (stress) | 20,000 | 0.020 | 1 | 400.0 | 380.0 | 506.0 | 43.7 |
| S5: Max targets (stress) | 20,000 | 0.020 | 2 | 800.0 | 760.0 | 1,012.0 | 87.4 |

Notes
- S4/S5 are intentionally “approval required” configs; the point is to show why the guardrails exist.
- If we later enable embeddings scoring, redo S3+ because embeddings QPS is often higher.


2) Scoring compute sizing (CPU + GPU)
We size scoring based on score_jobs_per_second ≈ score_eps.

CPU
- CPU_seconds_per_second = score_eps * CPU_time_per_job
- CPU cores needed ≈ CPU_seconds_per_second / target_utilization
  - target_utilization ~ 0.65 to keep tail + GC under control

GPU
- Effective_GPU_seconds_per_second = score_eps * (gpu_fraction * GPU_time_per_graded_job)
- GPUs needed ≈ Effective_GPU_seconds_per_second / target_gpu_utilization
  - target_gpu_utilization ~ 0.70 (room for batching variance)

Compute table (using CPU_time=25ms, GPU_time_graded=250ms, gpu_fraction=0.25, utilization CPU=0.65, GPU=0.70)

| Scenario | score_eps | CPU sec/sec | CPU cores (65%) | Effective GPU sec/sec | GPUs (70%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| S1 | 7.1 | 0.18 | 0.3 | 0.44 | 0.7 |
| S2 | 14.3 | 0.36 | 0.6 | 0.89 | 1.3 |
| S3 | 95.0 | 2.38 | 3.7 | 5.94 | 8.5 |
| S4 | 380.0 | 9.50 | 14.6 | 23.75 | 33.9 |
| S5 | 760.0 | 19.00 | 29.2 | 47.50 | 67.9 |

Interpretation
- Beta tenants are cheap: 1–2 GPUs per busy Dedicated tenant at default settings.
- Hosted aggregate at defaults is ~9 GPUs/region for model-graded at 25% coverage.
- Stress configs (2% sample, 2 targets) become very expensive quickly; breaker/backpressure must shed load before we ever get here.

Sensitivity knobs (product + ops)
- gpu_fraction: can cut GPU needs linearly (e.g., 0.10 instead of 0.25 reduces GPU by 60%).
- score_coverage: can be intentionally reduced under load (drop model-graded first, keep heuristics).
- t (shadow targets): multiplies everything.


3) Queue sizing and freshness math
Queue definitions
- We treat each (pair_id, shadow_variant_id, rubric_version) as one scoring job.
- Queue lag (Wq) + service time (Ws) = scoring lag.

Targets / constraints
- Operational breaker: oldest enqueue age must stay < 30 min, or mirroring shuts off.
- Product SLO: p50 <= 10 min, p95 <= 60 min (but breaker is the hard stop).
- Therefore steady-state goal: keep p95 queue wait <= 15 min so we have headroom for (a) retries, (b) storage hiccups, (c) grader slowdowns.

Recommended capacity planning rule (simple, works well in practice)
- Provision scoring throughput to handle 2.0x peak score_eps at p95 without exceeding 10–15 min queue wait.
- Maintain a small buffer: allow instantaneous depth spikes, but cap backlog age.

Queue depth guidelines (per region)
Let:
- λ_peak = peak score_eps
- T = max tolerated queue wait in seconds (we use 900s = 15 min)
- Target max depth ≈ λ_peak * T

Example (Hosted region default S3)
- λ_peak ≈ 2x * 95 = 190 jobs/s
- Target max depth ≈ 190 * 900 = 171,000 jobs
- If depth approaches this and oldest-age > 20 min, we should be dropping graded scoring and/or opening circuit breaker.

Practical caps (so we don’t store infinite backlog)
- Soft cap: 100k jobs/region (start degrading: drop graded scoring first)
- Hard cap: 200k jobs/region (reject new scoring enqueues; routing should emit dropped_backpressure and stop mirroring if breaker sees oldest-age)


4) Backpressure strategy (who drops what, and when)
Principle
- Drop work as far “upstream” as possible and always protect control path.

A) Data plane (mirroring)
- If circuit breaker open for cohort: do not serialize shadow request, do not write artifacts, do not pick shadow targets.
- Breaker open conditions (relevant here):
  - scoring queue oldest-age > 30 min
  - telemetry ingestion delay p95 > 10 min (avoid runaway buffers)
- Outcome accounting:
  - shadow_dispatch_outcome=dropped_circuit_open or dropped_backpressure (counts as “accepted drop” per SRE doc)

B) Telemetry ingestion
- If ingest is saturated: prefer dropping analytics-only enrichment first (e.g., example drilldown joins), keep core shadow.pair.v1 minimal.
- Enforce cardinality allowlist at exporter boundary (“_other” mapping) to prevent series blowups from turning into ingest brownouts.

C) Scoring enqueue
Two-stage degrade (recommended)
1) Degrade model-graded scoring
- When queue depth > soft cap OR oldest-age > 10 min:
  - set gpu_fraction_effective -> 0 (temporarily)
  - emit scoring_outcome=ok for heuristic-only metrics; emit instruction_following.score as null/absent (tracked via coverage metric)
2) Shed all scoring
- When queue depth > hard cap OR oldest-age > 20 min:
  - stop enqueuing new jobs (return “accepted but dropped” with a counter)
  - routing breaker should soon open at 30 min oldest-age and stop mirroring entirely

D) Retry policy (keep it from self-amplifying)
- Retries: exponential backoff with max 2 retries for transient grader failures.
- If queue is in degrade mode, do NOT retry model-graded jobs (convert to heuristic-only and continue).

E) Observability signals we need (must exist before external beta)
- scoring_queue_depth (by region)
- scoring_queue_oldest_age_seconds (by region)  [breaker uses this]
- scoring_jobs_started/sec, scoring_jobs_completed/sec
- scoring_outcome breakdown: ok / error_transient / error_permanent / skipped_no_artifact
- graded_scoring_coverage (what fraction got instruction_following.score)
- drop counters: dropped_backpressure_total (enqueue) + dropped_circuit_open_total (routing)


5) Open questions / TODOs (for review)
- Confirm event size assumptions after we ship shadow.pair.v1 + shadow.score.v1 to dogfood (need a 24h sample + actual Snappy sizes).
- Decide default gpu_fraction for GA (beta proposal: 0.25; GA could be 0.10 unless customers explicitly enable “full rubric”).
- Clarify whether Hosted will run region-local scoring or centralize per geo (affects cross-region queueing + data residency).
- For streaming: quantify “skipped_no_artifact” rate once PR-24904 behavior lands; update score_coverage.

Owner notes (Nadia)
- This doc is intentionally conservative on peaks and assumes we’d rather drop graded scoring than increase fleet size during spikes.
- If Product wants “always-graded” scoring, we need a pricing/packaging hook + per-tenant GPU budget enforcement, otherwise S4/S5 becomes reality fast.
